children: , the chip-architecture powerhouse spanning smartphones, data centers and edge computing, climbed approximately 1.3% to $264.73 Wednesday. Investors are looking beyond cloud AI toward the next computing battlefield: robots, autonomous vehicles and intelligent industrial equipment.

Arm's physical-AI initiative already connects more than 80 companies through its Total Design ecosystem. Its new robotics capability framework aims to give developers a common software foundation across different Arm-powered machines. Management believes physical AI could become a $200 billion annual computing market during the 2030s. That is a huge prizeand Arm wants its architecture sitting underneath it.

The company delivered $1.29 billion in fiscal first-quarter revenue, a 22% increase, while data-center royalties more than doubled. The picture adds a valuation warning: Arm's $264.73 share price stands 37.59% above its $192.41 GF Value estimate. Arm has the reach to become a core physical-AI platform, but the stock already prices in plenty of success. The real test is whether rising robot and edge-device shipments can generate richer royaltiesnot simply more low-cost chips.

title: Arm's Rise Hides a $200 Billion Robot Bet
